title: Dynamic latency-variance penalty + soft-eviction region selection policy
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Replace brittle threshold-only region eviction with a telemetry-driven 'variance-penalty' that combines p50/p95 latencies with short-term variance (EWMA of latency variance) and network loss/jitter signals (MAD-smoothed). The new policy should: 1) avoid unnecessary full evictions by applying a soft-eviction weight decay to region selection probability; 2) escalate gracefully to hard fallback when sustained regressions cross defined SLAs; 3) be tier-aware (production vs canary vs dev) so higher tiers get stricter sensitivity; 4) map to fallback model variants automatically (e.g., when region penalty > X, route to cheaper/quantized variant in primary region before cross-pop failover).

Why different from existing approaches: many current tickets optimize scoring using percentile deltas or nethealth heuristics; this task explicitly factors in variance (burstiness) and network metrics using robust statistics (MAD) and introduces the concept of soft-eviction as a persistent but decaying routing weight adjustment. That reduces churn and cascades during short bursts while still satisfying latency SLOs across traffic cohorts.

Design summary:
- Inputs: p50, p95, packet_loss_rate, jitter_ms, recent_error_rate (1m, 5m, 15m).
- Smoothing: EWMA for p50/p95 with configurable alpha per tier; MAD for packet_loss and jitter to avoid skew from outliers.
- Variance Penalty Score (VPS): linear combination: VPS = w1*norm(p95_delta) + w2*norm(variance_ewma) + w3*norm(packet_loss_mad) + w4*norm(jitter_mad). Normalization uses rolling windows and baseline percentiles per POP.
- Soft-eviction: compute a weight multiplier in (0.0,1.0] applied to region selection probability: weight = exp(-lambda * VPS) where lambda is tier-dependent. Weight decays back to 1.0 with a configurable half-life if VPS subsides.
- Escalation: if VPS exceeds hard_threshold for T_sustain seconds and traffic routed to region exceeds minimal qps, trigger hard-failover to fallback POP or model variant per routing policy.
- Fallback mapping: fallback selection first attempts local model variant with smaller memory/quantization profile (e.g., quantized-8bit variant) before cross-region routing to preserve data locality and cost predictability.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit tests for VPS math, EWMA windowing, MAD computations, and weight decay logic.
- Integration tests verifying weight changes on synthetic telemetry spikes and that soft-eviction prevents immediate hard failovers for single short spikes.
- Load test (k6 or locust) demonstrating fewer cross-pop failovers during synthetic p95 spikes vs baseline policy (target: >=10% reduction in cross-pop failovers for identical spike patterns).
- Grafana dashboard + Alert: VPS per POP, soft-eviction weight, sustained hard-fail triggers.
- PR merged: routing-service feature branch with canary toggle.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Prototype VPS function within routing-service (unit-tested).
2) Add telemetry aggregator pipeline & MAD/EWMA helpers (configurable by tier).
3) Implement soft-eviction weight in RegionSelector and expose metrics.
4) Add fallback-mapping rules: model-variant mapping table + canary config.
5) Canary rollout to 5% traffic for 24h, monitor defined KPIs (p50/p95, cross-pop failovers, request errors).
6) Gradual ramp to 50% then 100% with progressive lambda tuning.

Observability and dashboards:
- New Grafana panel: VPS timeseries per POP, stacked decomposed signals (p95_delta, variance_ewma, packet_loss_mad).
- Console: per-customer routing breakdown showing when soft-eviction adjusted weights and fallback mapping decisions.
- Alerting: config for VPS > hard_threshold for 5m -> page on-call + annotate incident dashboard for root-cause analysis.

Rollout risk & mitigation:
- Risk: overly-aggressive lambda causes under-utilization of healthy POPs. Mitigation: tiered conservative defaults + canary with traffic split and real-time rollback toggle.
- Risk: noisy metrics from sampling windows. Mitigation: MAD + minimum-sample gating and backoff.
- Risk: model-variant fallback impacts quality. Mitigation: tie variant selection to per-customer quality profiles and add QA test prompts in canary.
acceptance_criteria: 1) VPS unit and integration tests pass in CI; 2) Soft-eviction weight metrics emitted for each region and logged to tracing spans; 3) Load test shows >=10% reduction in cross-pop failovers under synthetic p95 spike traffic compared to baseline; 4) Canary 24h shows no significant increase in request errors or drop in customer-facing p95 beyond SLA; 5) Rollback documented and teardown plan validated.
notes:
Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SR/Dynamic+Variance+Penalty+Design. Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/489. Load test artifacts: gs://redwood-loadtests/variance-penalty/2026-03-k6-report.html.
